chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Money spent on exploitation, not product, and doors closed to young talent
summary: He angrily says the industry spends on promoting punk and ignores abundant young talent, and wants people to act.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Is there in your view some energy force trying to counter than now?
Not anything strong or big that I'm aware of. I am trying on an old man's way, just to keep the stimulation there, as far as young people are concerned. I tell them to go out and fight.
You do that when you go into campuses and --
Damn right I do, and I'd be glad to make the loudest speech they ever heard, because I think it's very unfair, very unfortunate and it's full of shit.

You see, they've taken away any incentive for a Shredman Brothers of New England or a Tom Rockwell in New York or all the things (unintelligible) and reinvest and invest money in new groups and the whole idea, because they've proven in their way through the media of radio, and of the record industry, above all, --
Yes.

-- that Charlie Schwartz and Abe Lasvogel are no longer in existence, but Pinky Stupatz and so-and-so and the producers of the newest hot thing, which is called punk up yours. And they now have it all figured out and it's the

only way --
(End of Side One.)
-- great deal of concern from your part about --

Well, my God, you go out and you find a greater grouping of young people who have more to offer than ever before, with less doors to knock on. And this is wrong for the history of America, it's wrong for our future history of America.
Yeah.

It's as wrong as anything I have ever witnessed. In order to make a film today, it costs you -- well, you can make a film for a dollar or $3.80. But they'll spend four million dollars on exploiting a 3.80 film. Our whole perspective is like this, and above all, it started with the music. Now it's into films, now it's into everything else. Spend all the money on exploitation, don't worry about the product. They'll accept the product. Am I saying --
No, I understand what you're saying, but isn't this really in common with the other members of the other arts and the state of the arts, as having a --
Well, I'm not so sure. I'm not that familiar with the other arts.
Yeah, I know you aren't, but -- you know, so many of them have many of --

I'm only involved in the one that's most obvious, music, which you hear 24 hours a day. And if you never heard anything else in your life, you'll walk around with eight-piece beats to the bar in your head, right?
Right, right.

And they're all youth. And in spite of all that, that they were weaned on this and never allowed to hear anything else, we have a big influx of whole new young people who want to hear (singing) along with other things.
Yes.
So, Goddamn it, if somebody doesn't do anything about it, then we're dumber than I thought we were.
